questions.question: What is the speed of light in vacuum?
questions.explanation: Light travels at approximately 3 × 10⁸ metres per second in vacuum.

questions.question: Which of the following is a luminous object?
questions.explanation: The Sun produces its own light — it is luminous. Moon and mirror only reflect light.

questions.question: A shadow is formed when an object:
questions.explanation: Shadows form when opaque objects block light from reaching a surface.

questions.question: Which material allows all light to pass through?
questions.explanation: Clear (transparent) glass allows all light to pass through.

questions.question: When a light ray hits a mirror, it:
questions.explanation: Mirrors are highly reflective surfaces — light bounces back (reflection).

questions.question: What happens to a shadow when the light source moves closer to the object?
questions.explanation: Moving the light source closer makes the shadow larger.

questions.question: Translucent materials:
options: Allow some light but scatter it
questions.explanation: Translucent materials (like frosted glass, oiled paper) allow light through but scatter it so you cannot see clearly.

questions.question: What is the bending of light when it passes from one medium to another called?
questions.explanation: Refraction is the bending of light as it passes from one medium (e.g., air) to another (e.g., water).

questions.question: A pencil placed in a glass of water appears bent. This is because of:
questions.explanation: Light changes speed and direction when moving from water to air, causing refraction — making the pencil appear bent.

questions.question: Which colour of visible light has the longest wavelength?
questions.explanation: Red light has the longest wavelength in the visible spectrum.

questions.question: A solar eclipse occurs when:
options: Earth is between Sun and Moon
Moon is between Sun and Earth
Sun is between Earth and Moon
questions.explanation: A solar eclipse occurs when the Moon comes between the Sun and Earth, blocking sunlight.

questions.question: What device uses mirrors and lenses to see distant objects?
questions.explanation: Telescopes use combinations of mirrors and lenses to magnify distant objects.

questions.question: Light travels in:
questions.explanation: Light travels in straight lines — this is why we get sharp shadows.

questions.question: What happens when white light passes through a prism?
questions.explanation: A prism disperses white light into seven colours: VIBGYOR (Violet, Indigo, Blue, Green, Yellow, Orange, Red).

questions.question: Night vision in cats is possible because:
options: Cats have more rod cells that work well in low light
questions.explanation: Cats have many more rod cells (light-sensitive) in their eyes, allowing them to see in dim light.
